# Data-quality review: reconstructed book

**Owner:** QR (Derek) · **Status:** BTC-USD and ETH-USD reviewed Oct 11, 2026. ZEC, QNT, HBAR and APT are pending: their in-sample raw data must be downloaded after the Tardis transfer quota resets (~22:00 UTC daily). Running `scripts/week2_pipeline.sh` then regenerates the tables, and §5 must be filled in from them.
**Scope:** in-sample dates only (holdout untouched). Market data only; no labels or feature-label relationships.
**Generated by:** [studies/data_quality.py](./studies/data_quality.py) → [output/data_quality_by_day.csv](./output/data_quality_by_day.csv), [output/data_quality_summary.md](./output/data_quality_summary.md).

Covered here: BTC-USD on all 19 in-sample days and ETH-USD on 10 of 19 (the other 9 hadn't downloaded when the quota was hit). One HBAR-USD day (2025-03-01) was used for the trade-side check.

## 1. Verdict so far

The Tardis Coinbase feed, as reconstructed by `book/`, is **clean enough to use without filtering beyond `book_valid`**. Nothing found needs a code change or a data exclusion. The anomalies that exist are real market events or documented vendor reconnects, and both are already handled.

## 2. Gaps and resyncs

| | BTC-USD (19 days) | ETH-USD (10 days) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Vendor reconnects (snapshot after updates) | 21 | 5 |
| Total invalid time | 49.4 s | 21.1 s |
| Longest invalid stretch | 19.9 s (2026-02-01) | 9.0 s (2025-05-01) |
| Lowest daily `book_valid` share | 99.97% | 99.99% |
| Book updates skipped while waiting for a snapshot | 87 at the start of each day (pre-snapshot updates), plus resync windows | same |

- The worst day is BTC-USD 2025-12-01, with **10 reconnects** (10.3 s invalid). Each one is short (≤1.04 s). They come from Tardis's recorder, not the exchange, and the replay marks each as invalid from just after the last good message until the new snapshot.
- The replay never raised an invariant error: no negative sizes, receive time never decreasing.
- **Phantom deletes** (a delete of a level that isn't in the book, the sign of a lossy or conflated feed): **0** in the Tardis data checked (BTC-USD 2024-11-01: 14.9M deletes; HBAR-USD 2025-03-01: 4.0M deletes). Our own live feed shows 1–15% (docs/data.md §6), which is why it isn't used for research. Book files built by the pipeline record this per day.

## 3. Crossed books, staleness, spreads

| | BTC-USD | ETH-USD |
|---|---:|---:|
| Messages that left the book crossed or locked | **0** | **0** |
| Valid seconds with spread ≤ 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Valid seconds with no book message in the previous 5 s | 0 | 0 |
| Longest quiet spell inside valid data | 1.7 s | 2.0 s |
| Median spread | 1 tick (0.001 bps) | 1 tick (0.04 bps) |
| Share of seconds at 1 tick, median day / worst day | 85% / 48% | 53% / 16% |
| p99 spread (worst day) | 1.4 bps | 2.3 bps |
| Max spread | 20.5 bps | 12.1 bps |
| Seconds with spread > 50 bps | 0 | 0 |

**Implication.** BTC and ETH on Coinbase sit at a one-tick spread most of the time. In tick terms they behave like large-tick books, even though the tick is tiny in bps. Queue imbalance at the touch should matter for them. For contrast, HBAR-USD on 2025-03-01 had a median spread of 8 ticks and was at 1 tick only 2.7% of the time.

## 4. Outliers

**1 s mid returns.** 47% (BTC) and 30% (ETH) of 1 s mid returns are exactly zero. Among non-zero returns the robust SD is 0.45 bps (BTC) and 0.52 bps (ETH). The largest 1 s moves are 28.9 bps (BTC-USD 2026-04-01 12:44:57) and 43.8 bps (ETH-USD 2025-05-01 15:10:53). I checked the three largest by hand. Each coincides with a burst of trades (265–625 trades in that second against a baseline of 1–20) and a jump in book messages, and none reverts within 10 s. They are **real market events, not data errors**, so they stay in the data (no winsorizing, per spec §4).

**Top-of-book size.** The largest L1 size is up to 3,900× (BTC) and 22,700× (ETH) the median. These are large resting orders at the touch. QI is bounded in [−1, 1], so they don't create numerical problems. They are a reason to prefer rank-based ICs (Spearman) as the primary metric.

**Depth.** The book never had fewer than 3,891 populated levels on a side, so `depth_imb_10` will never be "short" for these two symbols.

**Tick size.** Constant at 0.01 on every day for both symbols.

## 5. Remaining symbols (to fill in after the pipeline run)

For ZEC-USD, QNT-USD, HBAR-USD and APT-USD, read `output/data_quality_summary.md` and check the same items. The ones most likely to differ for these thinner books:
- [ ] stale seconds and quiet spells (thin books can go several seconds without a message, which makes labels NaN under the stale-mid rule);
- [ ] spread outliers above 50 bps and crossed messages;
- [ ] tick-size changes over the two years (HBAR and APT especially);
- [ ] days with fewer than 10 populated levels on a side (sets `depth_levels_short`);
- [ ] phantom deletes (expect 0, as for BTC);
- [ ] trade-side consistency on one day per symbol (HBAR done: below).

## 6. Trade side

Tardis reports the aggressor side. Checked on HBAR-USD 2025-03-01 against the reconstructed book just before each trade: **239,480 of 239,480 trades at the touch are consistent** (buys at or above the ask, sells at or below the bid), 0 inconsistent, and 40 printed inside the spread. This also confirms that trades and book updates are correctly ordered in time.
